newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China deal spurs RSS3 play in Singapore rubber.
newsitem.headline: China deal spurs RSS3 play in Singapore rubber.

text.p: Talk that China may buy several thousand tonnes of rubber from Thailand triggered speculative play for RSS3 rubber on Tuesday in the Singapore rubber market for the second day running, dealers said.

"People were very uneasy about this news and played it safe by picking up material in case something comes out," a dealer said. "There's been no news yet and we understand a deal will only be reached in July."
Singapore rubber traders said China will probably buy up to 80,000 tonnes of rubber from Thailand for delivery in the last six months of 1997.
"There's a lot of play we saw in RSS3 rubber today," a dealer said. "Otherwise, trading was pretty flat."
Dealers said news of a possible Thai-China deal will help provide support for prices in the market, which have been hammered for months by poor consumer offtake.

At 0945 GMT, July RSS3 was seen at 117.75 U.S. cents a kg from 116.25 cents. September RSS3 was seen up 50 cents at 118.50 U.S. cents a kg. July RSS1 was seen unchanged at 167.25 Singapore cents (US$1.17) a kg. September TSR20 was seen also unchanged at 157.50 Singapore cents (US$1.10) a kg.
